text: That afternoon: Holmes declares the bell-rope a dummy
why: The story has already placed the visit to Stoke Moran in the early afternoon (¶82, ¶126), and Holmes says 'it's a dummy' at ¶149 in that visit.

text: What Holmes finds in the bedroom
why: Holmes has examined the room's floor, panelling, bed and bell-rope, and the only finding stated is that the bell-rope is a dummy.

text: What was the bell-rope put there for? — for show, to make the room look cared for
id: q.why_bell_rope=for show, to make the room look cared for
why: A non-functioning bell-pull is plausibly decorative, and the story has given reason for this idea: Holmes calls the bell-pull 'unnecessary' (¶148) and it was only fitted a couple of years ago (¶145).

text: What was the bell-rope put there for? — an unfinished job: it was never connected
id: q.why_bell_rope=an unfinished job: it was never connected
why: The story says the bell-rope 'goes to the housekeeper's room' (¶143), and Holmes's finding that it is a dummy makes 'never connected' a possibility the reader can consider; repairs are also under way (¶67, ¶132).
